correctness.rationale: Under complete ballots and horizon L>=n, singleton JR requires every voter to be satisfied at least once, which in turn certifies JR for every group. Start from any per-round welfare maximizer, including arbitrary ties. If u voters are unsatisfied and c have satisfaction one, there are at most c critical rounds protecting the latter, so a noncritical round exists. Flipping it satisfies all u and takes no voter's last satisfaction. If a is the smallest winning approval count in a noncritical round, d=u+c and n/2<=a<=n-d. The loss is at most 2a-n and total welfare at least (L-c)a+cn/2. Their quotient increases with a. Comparing its value at n-d to (n-2)/(L(n-1)) gives a nonnegative cross-product Ln(d-1)-c(n-2)(n/2-d), strictly positive for d>1. Thus for n>=3 equality requires u=1, c=0 and a=n-1, hence every round has n-1 winner approvals. If any round's loser had more than the one unsatisfied voter's approval, flipping that round would incur strictly less than n-2 loss. This forces the fixed exclusive minority and the complementary exclusive majority in every round; direct optimization gives the converse for either choice of majority label each round. For n=2 every noncritical flip has zero loss.
residual_risks: The packaged finite tests are not the proof for general n,L and do not separately check the every-optimum repair assertion. The analytic argument does check it. No generalization to abstention, smaller horizons or stronger axioms is validated.

General complete-domain JR bounds and related static constructions are antecedents, not proof of this classification. Novelty is not credited to the JR definition or the already shared polarized examples.
residual_risks: The primary literature search was bounded and did not rule out unindexed exact binary analyses. The date shared by 5ba780619e23 and the reviewed record does not establish relative priority.

value.rationale: Restricting an agenda to two alternatives changes the welfare cost of guaranteeing every voter a satisfactory round. The sharp loss comparison quantifies that change; the repair produces a feasible nearby outcome directly from any unconstrained optimizer, while the converse identifies exactly when the worst cost cannot be avoided. This is more informative than a static example or a better constant without a mechanism.
residual_risks: A one-round repair need not maximize welfare subject to JR in every profile. No guarantee is made for other representation axioms, incomplete approvals or online voting.
